title: Cohort-aware introspective KV quantization evaluation and rollback policy
creator: Ava Chen
description: Objective: Evaluate FP8/INT8/INT4 compression profiles applied to KV cache with a focus on per-request cohort behavior (prefix length, attention locality, token distribution) and design an introspective rollback policy that minimizes customer-visible quality regressions while maximizing GPU memory reduction and throughput gains. Background: Prior experiments focused on global quant sweeps and layerwise heuristics; this initiative profiles live traffic cohorts and tests targeted per-cohort compression + dynamic rollback thresholds to reduce false positives where INT4/INT8 would degrade output quality. Success criteria: net GPU memory reduction >= 28% on p4/p40 family for production trace; end-to-end latency increase <= 3%; drop in key quality metrics (token-level error, hallucination rate, top-k divergence) within allocated thresholds (per-cohort quality degradation <= 1.5% relative to baseline), rollout policy triggers properly for real traffic within 10 minutes of a detected regression.
experiment_plan: 1) Cohort definition: derive cohorts from production traces by prefix length (short/medium/long), KV reuse ratio (high/low), and request type (chat/complete/embedding-proxy).
2) Instrumentation: extend runtime telemetry to tag requests with cohort_id, compression_profile, and dynamic_rollback_flag. Emit per-request metrics to metrics pipeline (Prometheus+Loki+Snowplow).
3) Compression matrix: test {FP8, INT8, INT4} x {uniform layerwise, block-wise, residual-compensated} x {global, per-cohort}.

4) Quality signals: collect token-level log-likelihood delta, stop-token divergence, embedding drift (cosine delta vs baseline), hallucination rate vs reference set, and a lightweight LM-assisted plausibility scorer.
5) Memory/latency measures: track GPU memory footprint (MiB), peak allocation, kernel runtimes, and p99/p50 latency under synthetic traffic matching production QPS.
6) Rollback policy design: implement introspective monitor that computes cohort-level quality deltas over sliding windows (1k reqs / 10m). Define hysteresis+cooldown to avoid thrashing.
7) Canary & traffic ramp: start with internal canary customers -> 2% traffic cohort assignment -> 10% -> 50% with manual gates.
8) Safety: for cohorts with high regulatory/customers tagged (PII-sensitive), default to FP8 or higher; INT4 disabled by policy.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial cohort extractor prototype committed (analytics ETL) — PR linked. Metrics pipeline now emits cohort_id tag on synthetic runs.
2026-02-20: Baseline memory/quality numbers collected on p4 and p40 families for representative models (seq-lens 128/512/2048). Baseline artifacts uploaded to dashboard.

2026-02-28: FP8 + residual compensation evaluated per-cohort; FP8 shows ~22% memory savings with negligible token_ll_delta_mean on medium/short cohorts, but long-authored conversations show small downstream embedding drift (0.9%).

2026-03-05: INT8 uniform layerwise yields ~34% memory savings but introduces p95 token_ll_delta spikes for low-KV-reuse cohorts; introduced a per-cohort guard that keeps INT8 only for high-reuse cohorts.

2026-03-10: INT4 experiments (blocked intervals) show 48-52% memory savings in isolated cases but hallucination rate increases beyond threshold for long-cohort; flagged as candidate for 'experimental' only behind feature flag.
2026-03-12: Rollback monitor prototype merged to runtime with cooldown=5m, hysteresis window=2x sample; initial canary rollout scheduled for 03-16.
initial_findings: Preliminary experiments suggest a mixed strategy: FP8 + residual compensation as default per-cohort yields consistent memory wins with low quality impact; INT8 useful for high-KV-reuse cohorts (chat assistants, long context with repeated prefixes) but requires per-cohort gating; INT4 currently too aggressive for general production traffic and should remain behind opt-in flags for internal customers. Observability is critical — cohort tagging and rapid rollback reduced visible regressions in canary sims by ~80%.
tradeoffs_and_considerations: Quality vs memory: INT4 gives largest memory wins but risk of subtle semantic drift and hallucinations in low-reuse, long-context cohorts.
Operational complexity: per-cohort policies increase routing/telemetry complexity and require careful indexing to avoid performance regressions in the runtime path.
Rollback sensitivity: aggressive thresholds reduce exposure but can negate memory gains if rollback triggers stably; hysteresis tuning needed.
Cost: memory savings translate to lower GPU unit costs; but added compute for residual compensation and monitoring increases per-request CPU overhead marginally.
decisions: Adopt FP8 + residual-compensation as the default KV compression profile across most cohorts for runtime-1.20.
Enable INT8 only for cohorts with measured KV reuse ratio > 0.65 and after passing a 50k-request cohort-level validation window.
Keep INT4 behind an internal feature flag; do not expose to customers until we have improved layer sensitivity heuristics and compensators.
Ship rollback monitor with default cooldown=5m and require manual approval to reduce cooldown in canary phase.
next_steps: 03-16: Start internal canary (2% traffic) for FP8 + residual-compensator across short/medium cohorts.
03-20: Run INT8 gated experiment on high-reuse cohorts for 50k requests, collect metrics and validate against thresholds.
03-24: Implement lightweight per-layer sensitivity probe to better estimate INT4 risk and iterate if safe.
Post-canary: prepare runtime-1.20 release notes, include rollback tuning knobs in Console rollout UI and expose cohort heatmap for SREs.
